Fullerene Charge Shuttle
LLM agents · deterministic code · LAMMPS — the model proposes, the code verifies

Two LLMs, one physics engine: a C60 shuttling between two nanotubes

The task: make a C60 fullerene oscillate between two capped carbon nanotubes held at opposite voltages, a nanometre-scale version of Franklin's electrostatic bell. NVIDIA Nemotron drove LAMMPS through four bounded tools and reached five crossings at 15 V on its ninth flight. Claude Fable wrote the simulation code and ran the 16 V flight shown here. In both cases the code, not the model, computes the charges and judges the result.

Mechanism

Why it oscillates

  • Charging. While the C60 touches a tube it sits at that tube's potential, so it takes a charge of the same sign.
  • Push and pull. Same sign as its own tube, opposite to the other one: it is repelled from behind and attracted ahead. Above the threshold this beats the van der Waals retention and it leaves.
  • Free flight. In the gap it is an isolated conductor: its charge stays constant. These are the flat steps of the charge curve.
  • Recharging. On touching the other tube it gives up its charge and takes the opposite one: the sharp spike.
  • Return. It runs down the tube, bounces off the cap, comes back to the mouth already carrying the right sign, and leaves again.

The voltage source pays at every transfer, roughly the charge carried times the voltage crossed, and little is dissipated. That is why the charge carried grows from one crossing to the next. Not checked quantitatively.

LLM agent · the model proposes, the code verifies

What the LLM tried on this task

Request in runs 1 and 2: find the lowest voltage that takes the C60 from one tube to the other without breaking it, starting at the mouth. Runs 3 and 4 were asked to make it oscillate, at least three crossings, with ten flights of up to 30 ps; run 4 was told the three crossings had to be in one long flight. Four bounded tools, and the verdict of each flight is written by the code, not by the model. The animation at the top is not one of these flights: it is the 16 V run set up with Claude Fable, which had the simulation code in hand and no flight budget.

Run 1: the model answered 14.2 V. That was wrong, and the fault was in the judge: a flight cut off while the C60 was still crossing counted as a failure, and "crossed, intact" did not require the C60 to be stopped in the arrival tube. Run 2, judge hardened: the model read each verdict and changed one parameter at a time, ran out of flights, and reported that it had found no working voltage. It invented no number. Run 3, ten flights and asked for at least three crossings: it found the set-up that works by itself, capped flexible tubes at 15 V, and the code returned "crossed intact". It then flew that same flight three times, one crossing each, and reported three crossings by adding them up. It never asked for a longer flight, which was allowed and would have shown whether the C60 really oscillates. Run 4, same budget, asked for three crossings in one long flight and for an explanation of the physics: on its ninth flight it flew capped flexible tubes at 15 V for 30 ps and the C60 made five crossings, intact. Checked independently on the trajectory. Its explanation got the caps and the flexible tubes right, but missed the point that makes it oscillate: it wrote that the field always pushes the same way, whereas the C60 swaps the sign of its charge at every contact (−1.17, +1.23, −1.19, +1.21, −1.48 e over the five crossings). One run per version: an observation, not a benchmark.

How it was computed

  • Geometry. Each (10,10) tube is closed by half a C240 fullerene, joined ring to ring and relaxed with AIREBO. Every atom has three neighbours except the 20 at the open mouth.
  • Charges. Method of moments with Gaussian charges: the tubes are held at +V/2 and −V/2. While the C60 is within Å of a tube it sits at that tube's potential; once clear, it is an isolated conductor that keeps its total charge.
  • Dynamics. LAMMPS, AIREBO with van der Waals plus Coulomb, 1 fs steps. All charges are recomputed every fs from the current positions.
  • Tubes. Free to vibrate and deform, held only by a two-cell ring at mid-length. Against perfectly rigid caps the C60 was destroyed on impact at every voltage tried.
  • Threshold. Static estimate: the voltage at which the electrostatic pull exceeds the van der Waals retention along the whole exit path, for a C60 starting at the mouth.

What this model does not show

  • One run per result, one voltage, started at 0 K. No statistics.
  • No field emission. The C60 carries more than one electron charge in a field near 1 V/Å; a real system would leak current before that.
  • Contact is a distance threshold, not a tunnelling model, and charge transfer is instantaneous.
  • The C60 speeds up from cycle to cycle. This may be energy fed by the voltage source at each transfer, or an effect of the update interval. Not resolved.
  • No trapping. With the voltage left on, the C60 never settles in one tube; it shuttles, then escapes.
  • Known artefact: deep inside a tube the C60 should be neutral (Faraday cage); with Gaussian charges it keeps a small charge of the opposite sign.
Computed with LAMMPS (AIREBO) and a NumPy charge solver. Mustapha Hamdi · mustapha.hamdi@innodeep.net
